[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: one variable 'remembers' everything that was put into it, so storing many values needs no special structure. Rule: a variable holds one value at a time; keeping many values for later use needs a data structure such as an array.

[0] names_the_element (N): Identity: a data structure is a method for organizing data; the one-dimensional array is the book's first example, and the two-dimensional array the second.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Declarative: an array is a data structure that stores a sequence of values of the same type and gives direct access to each by its index.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing: a structure is first built (for an array: declare, create, initialize) and then accessed one element per operation.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: what an array structure provides is fast access to any stored value: element i is found by adding i to the array's address.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: one array operation changes at most one element (an assignment) or creates a new array; reads change nothing.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): A data structure organizes many values of a data type; the array holds a sequence of values of one type, and its operations (create, index, length) work on that collection.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan/role: organize large amounts of data so it can be stored and then processed by indexing (vectors, matrices, tables, experimental results).

[0] predict_a_change (C): Conservation: choosing a different organization keeps the data but changes which operations are cheap. Using arrays enlarges the program state, so tracing becomes harder and invariants matter more.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Applicability: use an array when the number of values is known when it is created and access is by integer position. Other structures (Chapter 4) fit growing collections or non-integer keys.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Values needed again later must be stored in a structure, not a single variable. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: a task that needs a second pass over the data (e.g. count how many equal the maximum) is solved with one variable that keeps only the latest value
An array is a data structure: one name for a sequence of values of the same type, organised by index.
A data structure organizes many values of a data type; the array holds a sequence of values of one type.
